validity.recommendation: Rename / add OtherEnglishNames = 'Iranshahr–Chabahar–Konarak (Makran) Gas Pipeline'; fill blank endpoints (Iranshahr → Chabahar/Konarak, Sistan & Baluchestan) and add StartLocation/EndLocation refs. Keep as a segment distinct from P0446 (the Asaluyeh–Iranshahr main IGAT-7 trunk) — not a physical duplicate, but the shared name/gem.wiki page invites confusion.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED real. This row (P2015, segment 'Expansion', StartYear 2024, length 290 km) is NOT the IGAT-7 main trunk — it is the Iranshahr–Makran–Chabahar–Konarak gas transmission line that branches off IGAT-7 (and is tied to IGAT-11) at Iranshahr and runs south to the Makran coast. The sheet's own cited source (iranoilgas.com id=26497) is titled 'Iran's Iranshahr-Chabahar 290 km gas pipeline extension project from IGAT VII in Baluchestan province was officially [launched]' — confirming the 290 km and the Iranshahr–Chabahar identity. Independently corroborated by mizanonline (official inauguration 7 June 2024 by acting president Mokhber; 200 km of 56-inch + 90 km of 20/42/16-inch; $420M capex; operator National Iranian Gas Co) and by shana.ir #642658 (290 km Iranshahr-Chabahar-Konarak line, part of the 7th & 11th national trunk program, executed by Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co, an NIGC subsidiary; Konarak power plant fuel-switch worth ~$560k/day). Three independent origins (trade wire + judiciary news agency Mizan + oil-ministry SHANA) agree. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk. DUPLICATE CHECK: shares the gem.wiki page 'IGAT_7_Gas_Pipeline' and identical citation set with P0446 (IGAT 7 main trunk, Asaluyeh→Iranshahr, 907 km, 1800 MMcf/d) — but these are physically DISTINCT segments (main trunk vs. the new Iranshahr→Chabahar extension), so NOT a double-count. GulfPub tracks the same extension separately as 'Iranshahr to Chabahar Gas Pipeline' (180 km, 56-inch, op. Mokran Gas Transmission Pipeline Company) + a 12 km Chabahar–Konarak spur, which supports it being a real, separately-identifiable line. ATTRIBUTION: Owner NIGC is correct (executed by IGEDC / Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co, an NIGC subsidiary; GulfPub's 'Mokran Gas Transmission Pipeline Company' is the SPV, also NIGC-affiliated). FuelSource South Pars is consistent (the line is fed off IGAT-7 which carries South Pars gas). Main defect is naming/endpoints, not existence.

validity.recommendation: Clear ShelvedYear = 2012 — it contradicts Status=operating with StartYear1=2024. It is stale residue from the old (presumed-cancelled ~2010–12) IGAT-7 capacity-expansion-to-2.9-bcfd narrative, not the 2024 Chabahar extension this row now represents.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC/DATA-LOGIC contradiction: the row carries ShelvedYear=2012 (MISSING_REF) while Status=operating and StartYear1=2024 (both sourced). A pipeline cannot be shelved in 2012 and operating from 2024 under one record. The 2012 shelving refers to the abandoned plan to expand IGAT-7 throughput to 2.9 bcfd (OGJ 2010; no updates since), which is a different storyline from the Iranshahr–Chabahar extension inaugurated June 2024. ShelvedYear should be removed. LENGTH 290 km, StartYear 2024, Owner NIGC, FuelSource South Pars all confirmed (see attribution note). CAPACITY 1100 MMcf/d (≈31 mmcm/d) is plausible — press cites ~30 mmcm/d design throughput for the line — but I could not token-verify a single page stating the capacity number, so it stays UNRESOLVED (see fills).

fills.researcher_notes: Sheet had endpoints blank (Start=Asia, End=Asia). Line runs Iranshahr → Chabahar/Konarak in Sistan & Baluchestan; all three sources name the Iranshahr–Chabahar(–Konarak) endpoints. Konarak is the terminal spur beyond Chabahar.

Owner/operator is National Iranian Gas Co (NIGC); mizanonline names NIGC (شرکت ملی گاز) and CEO Majid Chegini, shana names the executor Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co (IGEDC), an NIGC subsidiary. GulfPub's 'Mokran Gas Transmission Pipeline Company' is the project SPV, also NIGC-affiliated — NIGC as 100% owner is correct.

GEM capacity 1100 MMcf/d ≈ 31 mmcm/d. Press summaries cite ~30 mmcm/d design throughput for the Iranshahr-Chabahar-Konarak line (≈1059 MMcf/d), which roughly corroborates the GEM figure, but I could NOT token-verify a single accessible page stating the capacity number (hamshahri/irna pages are JS-rendered and failed token checks). Left UNRESOLVED rather than pairing an unverified ref. Do not fill until a page explicitly stating the capacity is verified.

routes.end_name: Chabahar, Sistan & Baluchestan, Iran (with terminal spur to Konarak)
routes.corridor_desc: Branches off the IGAT-7 trunk at/near Iranshahr and runs ~290 km south-southeast across Sistan & Baluchestan through the Makran region to the coast at Chabahar, with a terminal spur to Konarak (Konarak power plant). Main line ~200 km at 56-inch; ~90 km of smaller-diameter (20/42/16-inch) sections/spurs. The exact alignment between Iranshahr and Chabahar is not published; corridor is bounded by the named cities (Iranshahr – Nikshahr – Chabahar/Konarak) and roughly follows that road corridor — endpoints are high-confidence, the intermediate trace is approximate.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from three independent sources naming Iranshahr → Chabahar → Konarak. Coordinates are the published decimal-degree locations of those well-known cities (Iranshahr ~27.20N/60.68E, Chabahar ~25.29N/60.64E, Konarak ~25.36N/60.39E, Nikshahr ~26.23N/60.21E on the intervening corridor) — not fabricated; the intermediate pipe trace is inferred from the city corridor, no GIS route sourced, so no waypoint on the pipe itself is invented.

summary: P2015 confirmed real (IGAT-7 Iranshahr-Chabahar-Konarak 290 km extension, operating June 2024) but mislabeled as generic 'IGAT 7 Expansion' with blank endpoints and a contradictory ShelvedYear=2012; distinct from P0446, not a duplicate.
